minutes.headline: Commission heard the final Marshall Park design and authorized three to five portable toilets at the beach.
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission met on Zoom. Landscape architects presented the final Marshall Park design with a phased plan. The commission then took up the recreation director's update, the Board of Health's removal of Little League's portable toilets, and beach-season plans. It voted on a skate park sign, two lifeguard hires and the beach portable toilets.

votes.motion: Authorize the skate park group, after verifying the sign conforms to town bylaws, to post a fundraising sign near the Marshall Park entrance on Route 2A.
Recommend to the town manager approval of two returning lifeguards, Ian Laundry and Mason Bowser.

Authorize the recreation director to contract with a vendor of his choice for three to five portable toilets at the beach, preferably at the far end with a gate installed, second choice the former playground area.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park final design total estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: The architects said the estimate including insurance, contingency and overhead is the figure heard, at prevailing wage. A line-item cost estimate will be sent to the commission.
figures_as_heard: five million seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: No per-phase figures yet; only the whole-project estimate exists, with some added cost for remobilization if phased.
Skate park construction is not in the park estimate. Fundraising figures were mentioned loosely and the member was unsure of them.
Quotes were given per unit with a delivery charge, for six units. Placing them would also lose parking.

budget_items.topic: Gate at far end of beach
budget_items.what_was_said: A quote for a gate came in under a stated amount as an alternative to barriers.
Two vendors quoted per 28-day cycle for ADA and regular units, plus a sink option. An extra cleaning costs more, and prices are rising.
Last year's fee was per student with a family cap per session. Possible adjustment to be taken up at the next meeting.
Little League has not finished paying last year's program fees and promised to send a roster to square up.
The 2020 resurfacing is out of warranty and failing. Its original cost was recalled as over a stated amount, on the 2020 capital plan.

decisions.decision: Architects will send the full cost estimate to the commission, which the chair will forward to the town manager to decide next steps.
Chair will invite skate park representatives to a future meeting to report on fundraising.
Next meeting set for the third Wednesday, May 18, at 7 pm on Zoom.
Recreation director to email the commission a written list of defined and exploratory programs.
Recreation director to look into umbrellas for lifeguard stands and pricing a job box for beach equipment storage.

what_happened.line: The commission authorized the recreation director to contract for three to five portable toilets at the beach, preferably at the far end behind a gate.
Landscape architects presented the final Marshall Park design with a phased plan; the full cost estimate will go to the commission and on to the town manager.
The commission voted to recommend two returning lifeguards to the town manager.
The commission authorized the skate park group to post a fundraising sign near the Marshall Park entrance once it is checked against town bylaws.
The Board of Health's removal of Little League's portable toilets was discussed; approval of minutes was held until the next meeting.

why_it_matters: Beach portable toilets, lifeguard staffing and Marshall Park's design and phasing touch what the town spends on parks and what residents can use this summer.
Marshall Park has only a whole-project estimate, with no per-phase costs yet, so any future funding request would rest on a figure not yet broken out.
